title: Evaluation Results - Why do models vary in speed and quality?
subtitle: View model comparison results in a simple, readable format.

dataset.heading: Evaluation dataset
dataset.description: This is the sample corpus used to test model answers and grading behavior.

explanation.title: What is this dataset and how was it used?
bullets: Each row represents one test case.
The dataset contains real questions, reference answers, and user answers.
For chat models, model answers are compared with reference answers.
For grading models, predicted grades are compared with human grades.
The dataset is a sample and should not be treated as complete coverage.

apertus.heading: Chat quality - Apertus-8B-Instruct
apertus.description: This tab summarizes how Apertus answered the evaluation questions.
apertus.chartAlt: Distribution of BERTScore F1 for Apertus chat answers

explanation.title: How to read these results
bullets: The table shows one row per test question.
Higher BERTScore, ROUGE, and BLEU usually indicate closer similarity to the reference answer.
Citation rate shows whether answers include source-backed information.
Small models can be faster but may struggle with complex or long-context questions.

llama.heading: Chat quality - Llama 3.3 70B
llama.description: This tab summarizes quality and behavior for the larger Llama model.

explanation.title: How to read these results
bullets: Larger models may produce more detailed answers.
They can be slower depending on GPU load and context size.
Use quality metrics together with human review.

kimi.heading: Chat quality - Kimi K2
kimi.description: This tab summarizes results for the cloud-backed Kimi model.

explanation.title: How to read these results
bullets: Cloud-backed models may vary in latency depending on network and provider conditions.
Compare response quality and speed before selecting the model for a workflow.
Use this tab to understand where Kimi performs well or weakly.

grading.heading: Grading - DeepSeek-R1
grading.description: This tab shows how close automatic grades were to human grades.
grading.chartAlt: Confusion matrix comparing human grades and predicted grades

explanation.title: How to read the grading results
bullets: Exact accuracy shows how often the predicted grade exactly matches the human grade.
MAE shows the average grading distance; lower is better.
Weighted kappa measures agreement beyond chance; closer to 1 is better.
The model grade should be treated as a decision-support signal, not as the final human grade.
